title: "Part 4 – Multiverse, inference and preregistration"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/trust-one-day.html#/part-4-multiverse-inference-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 4 opens on the chart that the class has just built and reads it against every justifiable analysis of the claim on these data. It then asks how much certainty a hundred thousand respondents give when they come from sixteen countries, turns to the two replications that SCORE ran on later rounds of the survey, and closes on the single analysis that you would defend, declared before it runs.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Multiverse](../../cases/trust/multiverse.qmd) and slides | Your own small multiverse, then the curve of the claim: the 192 specifications ranked from the largest estimate to the smallest, with the published result of the original author (OA), the two SCORE reproductions, the five analysts and the two replications placed on it. An optional pair of slides tells where the idea of a multiverse came from and draws the garden of forking paths. | 10 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/trust/multiverse.qmd#class-results) | Find your own mark among the exploratory results of the class. Then rerun `try_spec()` with the choices that you submitted and read your placement, the number of the 192 specifications whose estimate is larger than yours, and send it in chat when the facilitator says go. | 10 minutes |
| Slides | What moved the estimate: each option of the curve set beside its twins, and the curve coloured by the adjustment set, which carries nine tenths of its variance. | 6 minutes |
| Slides, with [the inference section](../../cases/trust/multiverse.qmd#inference) of the Multiverse page as the follow-up | Standard errors with sixteen countries: the reference specification under four rules of inference, why the respondents of one country are not independent pieces of evidence, the few-cluster problem and the wild cluster bootstrap, the result with each country left out in turn, and what the curve leaves out. | 12 minutes |
| Slides, with [the replications](../../cases/trust/index.qmd#sec-replication) on the case study as the follow-up | The two SCORE replications on later rounds of the ESS, the three Rs on this paper, and why a claim that passes all three still leaves its causal reading untested. | 8 minutes |
| Slides, with [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd) as the follow-up | The critics of the multiverse, the argument that a fully specified question has one correct analysis and how anyone would identify it, what preregistration settles and what it leaves open, and the difference between the exploration of Task 4 and the declaration of Task 5. | 8 minutes |
| Slides, with [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) as the follow-up | Where a reanalysis is archived and registered, the preregistration of Multi100 itself, the two preregistration templates, the public record of the case with a three-minute search of the Multi100 component, and the eight AsPredicted questions mapped onto the decisions that you have already met. | 6 minutes |
| The preregistration block in your report, or [Browser lab](../../cases/trust/lab.qmd#task-5-preregistration) Task 5 | Complete the preregistration block before you run anything: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, one option for each decision, a sentence from your causal graph on why the specification answers the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. Render the report, or on the browser lab page copy the completed cell into your notes, and type "declared" in chat. When the class has declared, fit the specification with `run_spec()` and send it with `report_result()`. Your declared result is drawn on the chart as a filled circle beside the open circles of Task 4. | 22 minutes |
| Slides and [Multiverse](../../cases/trust/multiverse.qmd#class-results) | Two points from the literature, the single analytical path, what you take with you and the feedback form, with the class chart on screen. | 8 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have your own placement among the 192 specifications of the curve, one specification fixed in the preregistration block of your report before it was run, a report of your own that contains the result of that specification, and a view of what a result that is robust, replicated and still only an association does and does not say about its cause.
